stem: Before patient-specific culture results are available, a hospital team reviews the facility antibiogram when choosing empiric therapy. What information does this tool provide?

options.A: Aggregate local susceptibility percentages for organism-antimicrobial combinations that can help guide empiric antibiotic selection.
options.B: The current patient's individual allergy history and prior adverse drug reactions.
options.C: A definitive susceptibility result for the current patient's infecting organism before that organism has been cultured.
options.D: Hospital medication acquisition costs without microbiologic susceptibility information.

rationale: A is correct. CDC's NHSN Antimicrobial Resistance guidance describes a facility-wide antibiogram as a table of calculated percent susceptible values for organism-antimicrobial combinations and states that antibiogram data can be used to guide empirical antimicrobial therapy. B is patient-specific history, not antibiogram data. C overstates what aggregate surveillance can provide; the antibiogram does not replace patient-specific culture and susceptibility testing. D describes financial information rather than a microbiology susceptibility summary.
educational_objective: Use the hospital antibiogram as an aggregate summary of local organism-antibiotic susceptibility patterns to inform empiric therapy while still incorporating infection site, patient factors, and patient-specific culture/susceptibility results when available.
source_organization: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC), National Healthcare Safety Network
source_document_title: FAQs: Antimicrobial Resistance (AR) Option; MDRO Management — Summary of Recommendations
source_version_date: CDC NHSN AR FAQ dated 2025/current page accessed 2026-08-17; MDRO recommendations current page accessed 2026-08-17
source_locator: NHSN AR Option FAQ Q9: facility-wide antibiogram displays calculated percent susceptible (%S) for each organism-antimicrobial combination; NHSN/CLSI antibiograms can be used to guide selection of empirical antimicrobial therapy. MDRO Management V.A.3.a: hospitals and LTCFs should review local susceptibility patterns (antibiograms) to foster appropriate antimicrobial use.
source_claim_supported: A hospital antibiogram summarizes aggregate local antimicrobial susceptibility percentages and can inform empiric antimicrobial selection, but it is not an individual patient's susceptibility test.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: use infection-control and microbiologic information to support safe, evidence-based care and antimicrobial stewardship.
blueprint_topic: Safety and Infection Prevention and Control — interpreting facility antibiograms
correction_summary: Rebuilt the raw definition item into an empiric-therapy decision and added the key limitation that an antibiogram is aggregate facility data, not a substitute for the current patient's culture and susceptibility results.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Verified against current CDC NHSN AR Option FAQ and CDC MDRO antimicrobial-use recommendations.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: A accurately describes aggregate percent-susceptible data and its empiric role. B is patient history. C falsely converts population-level surveillance into patient-specific testing. D omits microbiologic data entirely.
audit_findings.choice_B: Incorrect; allergies are obtained from the patient record/history.
audit_findings.choice_C: Incorrect; patient-specific susceptibility requires culture/testing of that patient's isolate.
audit_findings.choice_D: Incorrect; an antibiogram is not a cost report.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A describes the actual data type and its supported clinical use.
audit_findings.cueing: All choices describe types of information a hospital tool might provide.
audit_findings.blueprint: Local susceptibility information supports safe infection management and stewardship.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Rechecked specimen-site limitations and avoided claiming a facility antibiogram predicts every infection site equally. The objective explicitly retains infection-site and patient-specific context. No second answer remained.
